questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x) = x^3 + \dfrac{3}{2}x^2 + 3x + 3$, then $f(x)$ is
questions.solution:
Given function is $f(x) = x^3 + \dfrac{3}{2}x^2 + 3x + 3$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = 3x^2 + 3x + 3$

$f'(x) = 3(x^2 + x + 1)$

The discriminant of the quadratic $x^2 + x + 1$ is $D = 1^2 - 4(1)(1) = -3 < 0$.

Since the leading coefficient is positive and $D < 0$, $x^2 + x + 1 > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Therefore, $f'(x) > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

This implies that $f(x)$ is an increasing function.

Answer: Increasing function

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An open hemispherical storage tank has radius 13 m. Oil flows into the tank such that the depth '$h$' of oil in the tank changes at the rate of 3 m / hr. When the depth $h = 1$m, the rate of change of the area of the top surface of the oil is
questions.solution:
Let $R$ be the radius of the hemispherical tank, so $R = 13$ m.

Let $r$ be the radius of the top surface of the oil at depth $h$. The distance from the center of the hemisphere to the oil surface is $R - h$.

Using the Pythagorean theorem in the cross-section of the hemisphere:

$r^2 + (R - h)^2 = R^2$

$r^2 = R^2 - (R^2 - 2Rh + h^2) = 2Rh - h^2$

The area of the top surface of the oil is $A = \pi r^2$.

$A = \pi(2Rh - h^2)$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \pi(2R - 2h)\dfrac{dh}{dt}$

Given $R = 13$ m, $h = 1$ m, and $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = 3$ m/hr, substituting these values gives:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \pi(2(13) - 2(1))(3)$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \pi(26 - 2)(3)$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 72\pi$ m^2$/hr

Answer: $72\pi$ m^2$ / hr

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The function $f(x) = e^{ax} + e^{-ax}$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a < 0$, is strictly decreasing for all values of '$x$', where
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = e^{ax} + e^{-ax}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = a e^{ax} - a e^{-ax} = a(e^{ax} - e^{-ax})$

For $f(x)$ to be strictly decreasing, $f'(x) < 0$.

$a(e^{ax} - e^{-ax}) < 0$

Since $a < 0$, dividing by $a$ reverses the inequality:

$e^{ax} - e^{-ax} > 0$

$e^{ax} > e^{-ax}$

Since the exponential function is strictly increasing, we can compare the exponents:

$ax > -ax$

$2ax > 0$

Since $a < 0$, dividing by $2a$ reverses the inequality again:

$x < 0$

Therefore, the function is strictly decreasing for $x < 0$.

Answer: $x < 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A movie screen on a wall is 20 feet high and 10 feet above the floor. What is the maximum viewing angle $\theta$ (in radians) that can be achieved by positioning yourself at the optimal distance from the wall?
questions.solution:
Let $x$ be the distance of the observer from the wall.

Let $\alpha$ be the angle of elevation to the bottom of the screen and $\beta$ be the angle of elevation to the top of the screen.

The height of the bottom of the screen is $10$ feet and the height of the top of the screen is $10 + 20 = 30$ feet.

From the geometry of the setup, we have $\tan \alpha = \dfrac{10}{x}$ and $\tan \beta = \dfrac{30}{x}$.

The viewing angle is $\theta = \beta - \alpha$.

$\tan \theta = \tan(\beta - \alpha) = \dfrac{\tan \beta - \tan \alpha}{1 + \tan \beta \tan \alpha}$

Substituting the values, we get:

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{\dfrac{30}{x} - \dfrac{10}{x}}{1 + \left(\dfrac{30}{x}\right)\left(\dfrac{10}{x}\right)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{20}{x}}{\dfrac{x^2 + 300}{x^2}} = \dfrac{20x}{x^2 + 300}$

To maximize $\theta$, we must maximize $\tan \theta$ since $\theta$ is an acute angle.

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{20}{x + \dfrac{300}{x}}$

Using the AM-GM inequality for $x > 0$, the minimum value of the denominator is:

$x + \dfrac{300}{x} \ge 2\sqrt{x \cdot \dfrac{300}{x}} = 2\sqrt{300} = 20\sqrt{3}$

The maximum value of $\tan \theta$ is therefore $\dfrac{20}{20\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

This maximum occurs when $x = \dfrac{300}{x} \Rightarrow x = 10\sqrt{3}$ feet.

Thus, $\tan \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The absolute maximum and minimum values of the function $f(x) = \sin x + \sqrt{3}\cos x$ in $[0, \pi]$ are
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \sin x + \sqrt{3}\cos x$

We can rewrite the function as:

$f(x) = 2 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \sin x + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cos x \right) = 2 \sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

For $x \in [0, \pi]$, the angle $\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right]$.

The maximum value of $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ in this interval is $1$, which occurs at $x + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Thus, the absolute maximum value of $f(x)$ is $2 \times 1 = 2$.

The minimum value of $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ in this interval occurs at the endpoint $x + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3} \Rightarrow x = \pi$.

Thus, the absolute minimum value of $f(x)$ is $2 \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) = 2 \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{3}$.

Alternatively, evaluating the function at the critical point $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and the endpoints $x = 0, \pi$:

$f(0) = \sqrt{3}$

$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 2$

$f(\pi) = -\sqrt{3}$

Therefore, the absolute minimum value is $-\sqrt{3}$ and the absolute maximum value is $2$.

Answer: Minimum value $= -\sqrt{3}$, maximum value $= 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A square plate is contracting at a uniform rate of 2 $\text{cm}^2$ / min. The rate at which the perimeter is decreasing when the side of the square is 16 cm is:
questions.solution:
Let $x$ be the side length of the square plate.

Area of the square, $A = x^2$

Perimeter of the square, $P = 4x$

Given that the area is contracting at a uniform rate of $2\ \text{cm}^2/\text\min$, we have:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -2$

Differentiating $A = x^2$ with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 2x \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

Substituting $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -2$ and $x = 16$:

$-2 = 2(16) \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{16}\ \text{cm}/\text\min$

Now, differentiating $P = 4x$ with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 4 \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

Substituting the value of $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$:

$\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 4 \left(-\dfrac{1}{16}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{4}\ \text{cm}/\text\min$

The negative sign indicates that the perimeter is decreasing. Therefore, the rate at which the perimeter is decreasing is $\dfrac{1}{4}\ \text{cm}/\text\min$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{4}\ cm\ /\ min$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If 3 cm/s is the rate at which the side of an equilateral triangle increases, then the rate of change of area, when the side is 12 cm is:
questions.solution:
Let the side of the equilateral triangle be $a$ and its area be $A$.

The area of an equilateral triangle is given by $A = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2$.

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 2a \times \dfrac{da}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a \dfrac{da}{dt}$

Given that $\dfrac{da}{dt} = 3 \text{ cm/s}$ and $a = 12 \text{ cm}$, substituting these values:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 12 \times 3 = 18\sqrt{3} \text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$

Answer: $18\sqrt{3} \ \text{cm}^2 / \text{s}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The behaviour of the function $f(x) = \sin \left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) on \left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}$ , $\dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$ is:
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \sin\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = 2\cos\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

For the given interval $x \in \left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}, \dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$:

$\dfrac{3\pi}{4} < 2x < \dfrac{5\pi}{4}$

$\dfrac{3\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} < 2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4} < \dfrac{5\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$\pi < 2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4} < \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$

In the interval $\left(\pi, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, the cosine function is negative.

Therefore, $\cos\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) < 0 \Rightarrow f'(x) < 0$

Hence, $f(x)$ is strictly decreasing on $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}, \dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$.

Answer: Strictly decreasing on $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8} , \dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the function $f(x) = x^4 - 31x^2 + ax + 5$ has a turning point at $x = 1$, then the value of '$a$' is ___ and the function attains a ___ at $ x = 1$
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = x^4 - 31x^2 + ax + 5$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = 4x^3 - 62x + a$

Since $f(x)$ has a turning point at $x = 1$, $f'(1) = 0$

$4(1)^3 - 62(1) + a = 0$

$a = 58$

Now, finding the second derivative:

$f''(x) = 12x^2 - 62$

At $x = 1$, $f''(1) = 12(1)^2 - 62 = -50$

Since $f''(1) < 0$, the function attains a local maxima at $x = 1$.

Answer: $a = 58$ , local maxima

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A cone whose height is always equal to its diameter is increasing in volume at the rate of $40 \mathrm{ cm}^3 / \mathrm\sec$. The rate at which the radius is increasing when its circular base is $1 \mathrm{ m}^2$ is
questions.solution:
Given the height $h$ of the cone is equal to its diameter $d = 2r$, so $h = 2r$.

The volume of the cone is $V = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi r^2 (2r) = \dfrac{2}{3} \pi r^3$.

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3} \pi (3r^2) \dfrac{dr}{dt} = 2 \pi r^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

Given $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 40 \text{ cm}^3/\text\sec$. The area of the base is $A = \pi r^2 = 1 \text{ m}^2 = 10000 \text{ cm}^2$.

Substituting $A = \pi r^2 = 10000$ into the derivative equation: $40 = 2 \times (10000) \times \dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

Solving for $\dfrac{dr}{dt}$: $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{40}{20000} = \dfrac{4}{2000} = \dfrac{1}{500} = 0.002 \text{ cm/sec}$.

Answer: $0.002 \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm\sec$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The two equal sides of an isosceles triangle with a fixed base 'b' cm are decreasing at the rate of $4 \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm\sec$. The rate at which the area is decreasing when each of the equal sides becomes equal to the base is
questions.solution:
Let the equal sides of the isosceles triangle be $x$ and the base be $b$. The height $h$ of the triangle is given by $h = \sqrt{x^2 - (b/2)^2} = \sqrt{x^2 - b^2/4}$.

The area $A$ of the triangle is $A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times b \times h = \dfrac{b}{2} \sqrt{x^2 - \dfrac{b^2}{4}}$.

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{b}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x^2 - b^2/4}} \times 2x \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{bx}{2\sqrt{x^2 - b^2/4}} \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

Given $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = -4$ cm/sec and we need the rate of change when $x = b$.

Substituting $x = b$ into the expression for $\dfrac{dA}{dt}$:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{b(b)}{2\sqrt{b^2 - b^2/4}} (-4) = \dfrac{b^2}{2\sqrt{3b^2/4}} (-4) = \dfrac{b^2}{2(b\sqrt{3}/2)} (-4) = \dfrac{b^2}{b\sqrt{3}} (-4) = -\dfrac{4b}{\sqrt{3}}$.

The area is decreasing at the rate of $\dfrac{4b}{\sqrt{3}}$ cm$^2$/sec.

Answer: $\dfrac{4 b}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $x=a(\theta+\sin \theta)$ and $y=a(1-\cos \theta)$ represents the equation of a curve. If $\theta$ changes at a constant rate $k$ then the rate of change of the slope of the tangent to the curve at $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ is
questions.solution:
Given $x = a(\theta + \sin \theta)$ and $y = a(1 - \cos \theta)$.

The slope of the tangent is $m = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}$.

Calculating derivatives with respect to $\theta$:
$\dfrac{dy}{d\theta} = a \sin \theta$
$\dfrac{dx}{d\theta} = a(1 + \cos \theta)$

Thus, $m = \dfrac{a \sin \theta}{a(1 + \cos \theta)} = \dfrac{2 \sin(\theta/2) \cos(\theta/2)}{2 \cos^2(\theta/2)} = \tan(\theta/2)$.

We need the rate of change of the slope with respect to time $t$, which is $\dfrac{dm}{dt} = \dfrac{dm}{d\theta} \times \dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$.

Given $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = k$, we have $\dfrac{dm}{d\theta} = \dfrac{d}{d\theta} \tan(\theta/2) = \dfrac{1}{2} \sec^2(\theta/2)$.

At $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, $\theta/2 = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

$\dfrac{dm}{d\theta} = \dfrac{1}{2} \sec^2(\pi/6) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{dm}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times k = \dfrac{2k}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2 k}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The curve $4 y=3 x^4-2 x^2$ attains -------- at the points $x=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $x=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
options: a minimum value and a maximum value respectively
a maximum value and a minimum value respectively
questions.solution:
Given the curve $4y = 3x^4 - 2x^2$, we have $y = \dfrac{3}{4}x^4 - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2$.

To find the critical points, we calculate the first derivative with respect to $x$:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{4}(4x^3) - \dfrac{1}{2}(2x) = 3x^3 - x = x(3x^2 - 1)$.

Setting $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$, we get $x = 0$, $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, and $x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

To determine the nature of these points, we calculate the second derivative:
$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 9x^2 - 1$.

Evaluating at $x = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$:
$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 9\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) - 1 = 3 - 1 = 2$.

Since $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} > 0$ at both $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, the function attains a local minimum value at both points.

Answer: both minimum values

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Quadrilateral PQRS is inscribed inside a rectangle of dimensions $10 \mathrm{ cm} \times 8 \mathrm{ cm}$. The value of ' $x$ ', if the area of the quadrilateral is minimum is
questions.solution:
Let the rectangle be $ABCD$ with $AB = CD = 10$ cm and $AD = BC = 8$ cm. Let $AQ = x$, $BR = x$, $CS = x$, and $DP = x$.

The points are located as follows: $Q$ is on $AB$ such that $AQ = x$, so $QB = 10 - x$. $R$ is on $BC$ such that $BR = x$, so $RC = 8 - x$. $S$ is on $CD$ such that $CS = x$, so $DS = 10 - x$. $P$ is on $AD$ such that $DP = x$, so $AP = 8 - x$.

The area of the quadrilateral $PQRS$ is the area of the rectangle $ABCD$ minus the sum of the areas of the four right-angled triangles at the corners: $\triangle APQ$, $\triangle BQR$, $\triangle CRS$, and $\triangle DSP$.

Area of $\triangle APQ = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AP \times AQ = \dfrac{1}{2}(8 - x)x = 4x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}$.
Area of $\triangle BQR = \dfrac{1}{2} \times BQ \times BR = \dfrac{1}{2}(10 - x)x = 5x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}$.
Area of $\triangle CRS = \dfrac{1}{2} \times RC \times CS = \dfrac{1}{2}(8 - x)x = 4x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}$.
Area of $\triangle DSP = \dfrac{1}{2} \times DS \times DP = \dfrac{1}{2}(10 - x)x = 5x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}$.

Sum of areas of the four triangles $= 2(4x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}) + 2(5x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}) = 8x - x^2 + 10x - x^2 = 18x - 2x^2$.

Area of $PQRS = 10 \times 8 - (18x - 2x^2) = 80 - 18x + 2x^2$.

To find the minimum area, differentiate with respect to $x$ and set to zero:
$\dfrac{d}{dx}(80 - 18x + 2x^2) = -18 + 4x = 0$.

$4x = 18 \Rightarrow x = 4.5$ cm.

Answer: 4.5 cm

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In the interval $(0,1)$ the function $f(x)=x^2-x+1$ is
questions.solution:
The function is given by $f(x) = x^2 - x + 1$.

To determine the monotonicity of the function, we find its derivative with respect to $x$:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2 - x + 1) = 2x - 1$.

We analyze the sign of $f'(x)$ in the interval $(0, 1)$.

For $0 < x < \dfrac{1}{2}$, $2x < 1$, which implies $2x - 1 < 0$. Thus, $f'(x) < 0$ in the interval $(0, \dfrac{1}{2})$, meaning the function is strictly decreasing in this sub-interval.

For $\dfrac{1}{2} < x < 1$, $2x > 1$, which implies $2x - 1 > 0$. Thus, $f'(x) > 0$ in the interval $(\dfrac{1}{2}, 1)$, meaning the function is strictly increasing in this sub-interval.

Since the derivative changes sign within the interval $(0, 1)$, the function is neither increasing nor decreasing on the entire interval $(0, 1)$.

Answer: Neither increasing nor decreasing

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the function $f(x)=\mu \sin x+\dfrac{1}{3} \sin 3 x$ has its derivative equal to zero at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, then the value of ' $\mu$ ' is
questions.solution:
The given function is $f(x) = \mu \sin x + \dfrac{1}{3} \sin 3x$.

The derivative of the function is $f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx} (\mu \sin x + \dfrac{1}{3} \sin 3x) = \mu \cos x + \dfrac{1}{3} \cos 3x \times 3 = \mu \cos x + \cos 3x$.

It is given that $f'(x) = 0$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ into the derivative expression:

$f'(\dfrac{\pi}{3}) = \mu \cos(\dfrac{\pi}{3}) + \cos(3 \times \dfrac{\pi}{3}) = 0$.

Since $\cos(\dfrac{\pi}{3}) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\cos(\pi) = -1$, we have:

$\mu(\dfrac{1}{2}) + (-1) = 0$.

$\dfrac{\mu}{2} = 1$.

$\mu = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the length of the diagonal of a square is increasing at the rate of $0.1 \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm\sec$. What is the rate of increase of its area when the side is $\dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} \mathrm{ cm}$ ?
questions.solution:
Let $a$ be the side length and $d$ be the diagonal of the square. The relationship between the diagonal and the side is $d = a\sqrt{2}$, which implies $a = \dfrac{d}{\sqrt{2}}$.

The area $A$ of the square is given by $A = a^2$. Substituting $a = \dfrac{d}{\sqrt{2}}$, we get $A = \left(\dfrac{d}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{d^2}{2}$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$, we obtain $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2d \times \dfrac{dd}{dt} = d \dfrac{dd}{dt}$.

Given the side length $a = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ cm}$, the diagonal $d = a\sqrt{2} = \left(\dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \sqrt{2} = 15 \text{ cm}$.

The rate of change of the diagonal is given as $\dfrac{dd}{dt} = 0.1 \text{ cm/sec}$.

Substituting these values into the expression for $\dfrac{dA}{dt}$, we get $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 15 \times 0.1 = 1.5 \text{ cm}^2/\text\sec$.

Answer: $1.5 \mathrm{ cm}^2 / \mathrm\sec$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A man is moving away from a tower 41.6 m high at a rate of $2 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. If the eyelevel of the man is 1.6 m above the ground, then the rate at which the angle of elevation of the top of the tower changes, when he is at a distance of 30 m from the foot of the tower is
questions.solution:
Let $h$ be the height of the tower, $h = 41.6$ m. Let $h_0$ be the height of the man's eye level, $h_0 = 1.6$ m. The effective height of the tower above the man's eye level is $H = h - h_0 = 41.6 - 1.6 = 40$ m.

Let $x$ be the distance of the man from the foot of the tower. The angle of elevation $\theta$ is given by $\tan \theta = \dfrac{H}{x} = \dfrac{40}{x}$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$, we get $\sec^2 \theta \cdot \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -\dfrac{40}{x^2} \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

Given $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2$ m/s and $x = 30$ m. At $x = 30$, $\tan \theta = \dfrac{40}{30} = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Since $\tan \theta = \dfrac{4}{3}$, we have $\sec^2 \theta = 1 + \tan^2 \theta = 1 + \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)^2 = 1 + \dfrac{16}{9} = \dfrac{25}{9}$.

Substituting the values into the differentiated equation: $\dfrac{25}{9} \cdot \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -\dfrac{40}{30^2} \cdot 2$.

$\dfrac{25}{9} \cdot \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -\dfrac{40}{900} \cdot 2 = -\dfrac{80}{900} = -\dfrac{8}{90} = -\dfrac{4}{45}$.

$\dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -\dfrac{4}{45} \cdot \dfrac{9}{25} = -\dfrac{4}{5 \cdot 5} = -\dfrac{4}{125}$ rad/s.

Answer: $-\dfrac{4}{125} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm\sec$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A spherical snowball is melting such that its volume is decreasing at the rate of $1 \mathrm{ cm}^3 / \mathrm\min$. The rate at which the diameter is decreasing when the diameter is 10 cm is
questions.solution:
Let $V$ be the volume and $D$ be the diameter of the spherical snowball. The volume of a sphere is given by $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3$, where $r$ is the radius. Since $D = 2r$, we have $r = \dfrac{D}{2}$.

Substituting $r$ in terms of $D$, $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi \left( \dfrac{D}{2} \right)^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi \dfrac{D^3}{8} = \dfrac{\pi D^3}{6}$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi}{6} \times 3D^2 \dfrac{dD}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi D^2}{2} \dfrac{dD}{dt}$.

Given that the volume is decreasing at a rate of $1 \text{ cm}^3/\text\min$, we have $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -1$. We want to find the rate at which the diameter is decreasing, which is $-\dfrac{dD}{dt}$ when $D = 10 \text{ cm}$.

Substituting the values into the derivative equation: $-1 = \dfrac{\pi (10)^2}{2} \dfrac{dD}{dt} = \dfrac{100 \pi}{2} \dfrac{dD}{dt} = 50 \pi \dfrac{dD}{dt}$.

Solving for $\dfrac{dD}{dt}$, we get $\dfrac{dD}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{50 \pi}$.

The rate at which the diameter is decreasing is $-\dfrac{dD}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{50 \pi} \text{ cm/min}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{50 \pi} \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm\min$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The curve $a x^3+b x^2+c x+d$ has a point of minima at $x=1$, then
questions.solution:
Let $f(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d$. The derivative is given by $f'(x) = 3ax^2 + 2bx + c$.

Since the curve has a point of minima at $x=1$, we must have $f'(1) = 0$. Thus, $3a(1)^2 + 2b(1) + c = 0$, which implies $3a + 2b + c = 0$.

For a local minimum at $x=1$, the second derivative must satisfy $f''(1) > 0$.

The second derivative is $f''(x) = 6ax + 2b$.

Substituting $x=1$, we get $f''(1) = 6a + 2b > 0$.

Dividing the inequality by $2$, we obtain $3a + b > 0$.

Answer: $3 a+b > 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A solid S is made from a cylinder surmounted by a hemisphere on top with both its circular faces sharing a common centre. The radius of cylinder and radius of hemisphere are $x \mathrm{ cm}$. The height of the cylinder is $(20-4 x) \mathrm{cm}$ and the volume of S is $V=\dfrac{1}{3} \pi y$. Find the maximum value of $y$.
questions.solution:
The volume $V$ of the solid $S$ is the sum of the volume of the cylinder and the volume of the hemisphere.

Volume of cylinder = $\pi r^2 h = \pi x^2 (20 - 4x)$

Volume of hemisphere = $\dfrac{2}{3} \pi r^3 = \dfrac{2}{3} \pi x^3$

Total volume $V = \pi x^2 (20 - 4x) + \dfrac{2}{3} \pi x^3 = \pi (20x^2 - 4x^3 + \dfrac{2}{3} x^3) = \pi (20x^2 - \dfrac{10}{3} x^3)$

Given $V = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi y$, we have $\dfrac{1}{3} \pi y = \pi (20x^2 - \dfrac{10}{3} x^3)$, which implies $y = 60x^2 - 10x^3$.

To find the maximum value of $y$, differentiate with respect to $x$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 120x - 30x^2$.

Setting $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$, we get $30x(4 - x) = 0$. Since $x > 0$, we have $x = 4$.

Check the second derivative: $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 120 - 60x$. At $x = 4$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 120 - 240 = -120 < 0$, so $y$ is maximum at $x = 4$.

Substituting $x = 4$ into the expression for $y$: $y = 60(4)^2 - 10(4)^3 = 60(16) - 10(64) = 960 - 640 = 320$.

Answer: $320$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Oil from a conical funnel is dripping at the rate of $5 \mathrm{ cm}^3 / \mathrm{s}$. If the radius and height of the funnel are 10 cm and 20 cm respectively, then the rate at which the oil level drops when it is 5 cm from the top is
questions.solution:
Let $R = 10$ cm be the radius and $H = 20$ cm be the height of the conical funnel. Let $r$ and $h$ be the radius and height of the oil level at any time $t$. By similar triangles, $\dfrac{r}{h} = \dfrac{R}{H} = \dfrac{10}{20} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $r = \dfrac{h}{2}$.

The volume of the oil in the funnel is $V = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi \left( \dfrac{h}{2} \right)^2 h = \dfrac{\pi h^3}{12}$.

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi}{12} \times 3h^2 \dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi h^2}{4} \dfrac{dh}{dt}$.

Given $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -5$ cm$^3$/s (since the volume is decreasing). The oil level is 5 cm from the top, so the height of the oil from the vertex is $h = 20 - 5 = 15$ cm.

Substituting the values, $-5 = \dfrac{\pi (15)^2}{4} \dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{225 \pi}{4} \dfrac{dh}{dt}$.

Solving for $\dfrac{dh}{dt}$, we get $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = -5 \times \dfrac{4}{225 \pi} = -\dfrac{20}{225 \pi} = -\dfrac{4}{45 \pi}$ cm/s.

Answer: $-\dfrac{4}{45 \pi} \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The least value of ' $a$ ' such that the function $x^2+a x+1$ is increasing on $[1,2]$ is
questions.solution:
Let $f(x) = x^2 + ax + 1$.

The function $f(x)$ is increasing on the interval $[1,2]$ if its derivative $f'(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in [1,2]$.

Calculating the derivative, we get $f'(x) = 2x + a$.

For $f(x)$ to be increasing on $[1,2]$, we require $2x + a \ge 0$ for all $x \in [1,2]$.

This inequality must hold for the minimum value of $x$ in the interval $[1,2]$, which is $x = 1$.

Substituting $x = 1$ into the inequality, we get $2(1) + a \ge 0$, which simplifies to $2 + a \ge 0$.

Therefore, $a \ge -2$.

The least value of $a$ is $-2$.

Answer: $-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The slope of the tangent to the curve, $y=x^3-3 x^2 y$ at $(1,1)$ is

questions.q: Find the approximate value of function $f(x)=x^3-5 x+10$ at $x=3.001$.
questions.solution:
We can write 3.001 as x=3 and $\Delta x=0.001$ and use the relation

Now,

questions.q: Let $f(x)=5+(2 x-3)^{\frac{4}{3}}$, then the minimum value of $f(x)$ is
questions.solution:

$f(x)=5+(2 x-3)^{\frac{4}{3}}$
Differentiate w.r.t. $x$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The points on the ellipse $16 x^2+9 y^2=400$ at which the ordinate decreases at the same rate at which the abscissa increases are
questions.solution: The given equation of the ellipse is $16x^2 + 9y^2 = 400$.Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$, we get $32x \dfrac{dx}{dt} + 18y \dfrac{dy}{dt} = 0$.The problem states that the ordinate decreases at the same rate at which the abscissa increases, which means $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{dx}{dt}$.Substituting this into the differentiated equation: $32x \dfrac{dx}{dt} + 18y \left(-\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right) = 0$.Assuming $\dfrac{dx}{dt} \neq 0$, we have $32x - 18y = 0$, which simplifies to $16x = 9y$, or $y = \dfrac{16x}{9}$.Substitute $y = \dfrac{16x}{9}$ into the original ellipse equation: $16x^2 + 9 \left(\dfrac{16x}{9}\right)^2 = 400$.$16x^2 + 9 \left(\dfrac{256x^2}{81}\right) = 400$.$16x^2 + \dfrac{256x^2}{9} = 400$.Multiplying by $9$: $144x^2 + 256x^2 = 3600$.$400x^2 = 3600$, so $x^2 = 9$, which gives $x = 3 or x = -3$.If $x = 3$, $y = \dfrac{16(3)}{9} = \dfrac{16}{3}$.If $x = -3$, $y = \dfrac{16(-3)}{9} = -\dfrac{16}{3}$.The points are $\left(3, \dfrac{16}{3}\right)$ and $\left(-3, -\dfrac{16}{3}\right)$.Answer: $\left(3, \dfrac{16}{3}\right) \text{$ and }$\left(-3,-\dfrac{16}{3}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=\log x+b x^2+a x, x \neq 0$ has extreme values (or turning points) at $x=-1$ and $x=2$ then the values of $\mathrm{a}$ and $\mathrm{b}$ are
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \log x + bx^2 + ax$. The derivative of the function is $f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} + 2bx + a$.

Since the function has extreme values at $x = -1$ and $x = 2$, $f'(x)$ must be zero at these points.

For $x = -1$: $f'(-1) = \dfrac{1}{-1} + 2b(-1) + a = 0 \Rightarrow -1 - 2b + a = 0 \Rightarrow a - 2b = 1$.

For $x = 2$: $f'(2) = \dfrac{1}{2} + 2b(2) + a = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2} + 4b + a = 0 \Rightarrow a + 4b = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Subtracting the first equation from the second: $(a + 4b) - (a - 2b) = -\dfrac{1}{2} - 1 \Rightarrow 6b = -\dfrac{3}{2} \Rightarrow b = -\dfrac{3}{12} = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Substituting $b = -\dfrac{1}{4}$ into $a - 2b = 1$: $a - 2(-\dfrac{1}{4}) = 1 \Rightarrow a + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Thus, $a = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $b = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Answer: $a=\dfrac{1}{2} \quad b=-\dfrac{1}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\text{ The function } y=\tan x-x \text{$ is }
questions.solution:
Let $f(x) = \tan x - x$.

To determine the intervals of increase or decrease, find the first derivative of $f(x)$ with respect to $x$.

$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan x - x) = \sec^2 x - 1$.

Using the trigonometric identity $\sec^2 x - 1 = \tan^2 x$, we have $f'(x) = \tan^2 x$.

For $x \in (0, \dfrac{\pi}{2})$, $\tan x > 0$, which implies $\tan^2 x > 0$.

Since $f'(x) > 0$ for all $x \in (0, \dfrac{\pi}{2})$, the function $f(x) = \tan x - x$ is strictly increasing in the interval $(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2})$.

Answer: $\text{ an increasing function in } \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The dimensions of the largest rectangle of side $x$ and $y$ that can be inscribed in the right angled triangle of sides $\mathrm{a}$ and $\mathrm{b}$ is
questions.solution:
Let the right-angled triangle have base $a$ and height $b$. The rectangle is inscribed such that one vertex lies on the hypotenuse, and two sides lie along the legs of the triangle. Let the rectangle have width $x$ and height $y$.

Using similar triangles, the small triangle at the top has base $x$ and height $b - y$. The large triangle has base $a$ and height $b$. By similarity:

$\dfrac{x}{a} = \dfrac{b - y}{b}$

This simplifies to $x = \dfrac{a(b - y)}{b} = a - \dfrac{a}{b}y$.

The area $A$ of the rectangle is given by $A = xy = y(a - \dfrac{a}{b}y) = ay - \dfrac{a}{b}y^2$.

To maximize the area, we differentiate $A$ with respect to $y$ and set it to zero:

$\dfrac{dA}{dy} = a - \dfrac{2a}{b}y = 0$

Solving for $y$, we get $y = \dfrac{b}{2}$.

Substituting $y = \dfrac{b}{2}$ into the equation for $x$:

$x = a - \dfrac{a}{b}(\dfrac{b}{2}) = a - \dfrac{a}{2} = \dfrac{a}{2}$.

Thus, the dimensions of the largest rectangle are $x = \dfrac{a}{2}$ and $y = \dfrac{b}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{a}{2}, \dfrac{b}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\text{ If } f(x)=\dfrac{a \sin x+b \cos x}{c \sin x+d \cos x} \text{ is decreasing for all } x \text{,$ then }
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{a \sin x + b \cos x}{c \sin x + d \cos x}$.

To determine the condition for $f(x)$ to be decreasing, we find the derivative $f'(x)$ using the quotient rule $\left( \dfrac{u}{v} \right)' = \dfrac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}$.

Let $u = a \sin x + b \cos x$ and $v = c \sin x + d \cos x$.

$u' = a \cos x - b \sin x$ and $v' = c \cos x - d \sin x$.

$f'(x) = \dfrac{(a \cos x - b \sin x)(c \sin x + d \cos x) - (a \sin x + b \cos x)(c \cos x - d \sin x)}{(c \sin x + d \cos x)^2}$.

Expanding the numerator:

Numerator $= (ac \sin x \cos x + ad \cos^2 x - bc \sin^2 x - bd \sin x \cos x) - (ac \sin x \cos x - ad \sin^2 x + bc \cos^2 x - bd \sin x \cos x)$.

Numerator $= ad \cos^2 x - bc \sin^2 x + ad \sin^2 x - bc \cos^2 x$.

Numerator $= ad(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x) - bc(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x) = ad - bc$.

Thus, $f'(x) = \dfrac{ad - bc}{(c \sin x + d \cos x)^2}$.

For $f(x)$ to be decreasing for all $x$, we require $f'(x) \lt 0$ for all $x$.

Since the denominator $(c \sin x + d \cos x)^2$ is always positive, the condition $f'(x) \lt 0$ implies $ad - bc \lt 0$.

Answer: $a d-b c\lt 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The turning point of the function $y=\dfrac{a x-b}{(x-1)(x-4)}$ at the point $P(2,-1)$ is
options: neither a maximum nor a minimum
questions.solution:
Given the function $y = \dfrac{ax - b}{(x - 1)(x - 4)}$. Since the point $P(2, -1)$ lies on the curve, we substitute $x = 2$ and $y = -1$:

$-1 = \dfrac{2a - b}{(2 - 1)(2 - 4)} = \dfrac{2a - b}{1 \times (-2)} = \dfrac{2a - b}{-2}$

$2 = 2a - b \Rightarrow b = 2a - 2$

The function becomes $y = \dfrac{ax - (2a - 2)}{(x - 1)(x - 4)} = \dfrac{a(x - 2) + 2}{(x - 1)(x - 4)}$. Let $u = x - 2$. Then $x - 1 = u + 1$ and $x - 4 = u - 2$.

$y = \dfrac{au + 2}{(u + 1)(u - 2)} = \dfrac{au + 2}{u^2 - u - 2}$. For $P(2, -1)$ to be a turning point, the derivative $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ must be zero at $x = 2$, which corresponds to $u = 0$.

Using the quotient rule $\dfrac{dy}{du} = \dfrac{a(u^2 - u - 2) - (au + 2)(2u - 1)}{(u^2 - u - 2)^2}$. Setting $\dfrac{dy}{du} = 0$ at $u = 0$:

$\dfrac{a(-2) - (2)(-1)}{(-2)^2} = 0 \Rightarrow -2a + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow a = 1$.

Substituting $a = 1$ into $b = 2a - 2$, we get $b = 0$. The function is $y = \dfrac{x}{(x - 1)(x - 4)} = \dfrac{x}{x^2 - 5x + 4}$.

The second derivative test at $x = 2$: $y' = \dfrac{-(x^2 - 4)}{(x^2 - 5x + 4)^2}$. $y'' = \dfrac{-2x(x^2 - 5x + 4)^2 - (-(x^2 - 4)) \cdot 2(x^2 - 5x + 4)(2x - 5)}{(x^2 - 5x + 4)^4}$.

At $x = 2$, $x^2 - 4 = 0$, so $y'' = \dfrac{-2(2)(2^2 - 5(2) + 4)^2}{((2^2 - 5(2) + 4))^4} = \dfrac{-4(-2)^2}{(-2)^4} = \dfrac{-16}{16} = -1$.

Since $y'' < 0$ at $x = 2$, the point $P(2, -1)$ is a maximum.

Answer: a maximum

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\text{ The function } f(x)=\tan ^{-1}(\sin x+\cos x) \text{$ is an increasing function in }
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \tan^{-1}(\sin x + \cos x)$.

To determine the interval where $f(x)$ is increasing, we find the derivative $f'(x)$ and set $f'(x) \gt 0$.

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + (\sin x + \cos x)^2} \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x + \cos x)$

$f'(x) = \dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{1 + (\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x + 2 \sin x \cos x)}$

$f'(x) = \dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{1 + 1 + \sin(2x)} = \dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{2 + \sin(2x)}$

Since the denominator $2 + \sin(2x)$ is always positive for all real $x$, the sign of $f'(x)$ depends only on the numerator $\cos x - \sin x$.

For $f(x)$ to be increasing, we require $f'(x) \gt 0$, which implies $\cos x - \sin x \gt 0$.

$\cos x \gt \sin x$

Dividing by $\cos x$ (assuming $\cos x \gt 0$, which holds in the interval $(-\pi/2, \pi/2)$):

$1 \gt \tan x$

$\tan x \lt 1$

In the interval $(-\pi/2, \pi/2)$, $\tan x \lt 1$ holds when $x \lt \pi/4$.

Thus, the function is increasing in the interval $(-\pi/2, \pi/4)$.

Answer: $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the nature of the function $f(x)=x^3-3 x^2+4 x$ on real numbers?
questions.solution:
The function is given by $f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x$.

To determine the nature of the function, compute the first derivative with respect to $x$:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x) = 3x^2 - 6x + 4$.

Analyze the quadratic expression $3x^2 - 6x + 4$. The discriminant $D$ of this quadratic is given by $D = b^2 - 4ac = (-6)^2 - 4(3)(4) = 36 - 48 = -12$.

Since the discriminant $D < 0$ and the coefficient of $x^2$ is positive ($3 > 0$), the quadratic $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x + 4$ is always positive for all real values of $x$.

Because $f'(x) > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the function $f(x)$ is strictly increasing on the set of real numbers.

Answer: Increasing

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\text{ The rate of change of the volume of a sphere with respect to its surface area } \mathrm{S} \text{$ is }
questions.solution:
Let $r$ be the radius of the sphere. The volume $V$ and surface area $S$ are given by $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3$ and $S = 4 \pi r^2$.

From the expression for surface area, $r^2 = \dfrac{S}{4 \pi}$, which implies $r = \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{4 \pi}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\pi}}$.

Differentiating $V$ with respect to $r$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 4 \pi r^2$.

Differentiating $S$ with respect to $r$, we get $\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 8 \pi r$.

The rate of change of volume with respect to surface area is $\dfrac{dV}{dS} = \dfrac{dV/dr}{dS/dr} = \dfrac{4 \pi r^2}{8 \pi r} = \dfrac{r}{2}$.

Substituting the value of $r$ in terms of $S$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dS} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\pi}} \right) = \dfrac{1}{4} \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\pi}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{4} \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\pi}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The side of a cube is equal to the diameter of a sphere. If the side and radius increase at the same rate then the ratio of the increase of their surface area is
questions.solution:
Let the side of the cube be $a$ and the radius of the sphere be $r$.

Given that the side of the cube is equal to the diameter of the sphere, we have $a = 2r$.

Let the rate of increase of the side and the radius be $\dfrac{da}{dt} = \dfrac{dr}{dt} = k$.

The surface area of the cube is $S_c = 6a^2$. The rate of increase of the surface area of the cube is $\dfrac{dS_c}{dt} = 12a \dfrac{da}{dt} = 12(2r)k = 24rk$.

The surface area of the sphere is $S_s = 4\pi r^2$. The rate of increase of the surface area of the sphere is $\dfrac{dS_s}{dt} = 8\pi r \dfrac{dr}{dt} = 8\pi rk$.

The ratio of the increase of their surface areas is $\dfrac{dS_c/dt}{dS_s/dt} = \dfrac{24rk}{8\pi rk} = \dfrac{24}{8\pi} = \dfrac{3}{\pi}$.

Answer: $3: \pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=2 x^3+9 x^2+\lambda x+20$ is a decreasing function of $x$ in the largest possible interval $(-2,-1)$, then $\lambda$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = 2x^3 + 9x^2 + \lambda x + 20$.

The derivative is $f'(x) = 6x^2 + 18x + \lambda$.

For $f(x)$ to be a decreasing function, $f'(x) \le 0$ for all $x$ in the interval $(-2,-1)$.

The quadratic $f'(x) = 6x^2 + 18x + \lambda$ represents a parabola opening upwards. For it to be non-positive in the interval $(-2,-1)$, the roots of $f'(x) = 0$ must be $-2$ and $-1$.

If the roots are $-2$ and $-1$, then $f'(x) = 6(x + 2)(x + 1) = 6(x^2 + 3x + 2) = 6x^2 + 18x + 12$.

Comparing $6x^2 + 18x + 12$ with $6x^2 + 18x + \lambda$, we get $\lambda = 12$.

Checking the condition, $f'(x) = 6(x+2)(x+1) \le 0$ for $x \in [-2,-1]$, which satisfies the requirement.

Answer: $12$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The most economical proportion of the height of a covered box of fixed volume whose base is a rectangle with one side three times as long as the other, is
options: Equal to shorter side of base
questions.solution:
Let the sides of the rectangular base be $x$ and $3x$. Let the height of the box be $h$.

The volume $V$ of the box is given by $V = (x)(3x)(h) = 3x^2 h$. Since $V$ is fixed, $h = \dfrac{V}{3x^2}$.

The surface area $S$ of the covered box is $S = 2(length \times width + width \times height + height \times length) = 2(3x^2 + 3xh + xh) = 2(3x^2 + 4xh)$.

Substituting $h = \dfrac{V}{3x^2}$ into the surface area equation:

$S = 6x^2 + 8x \left( \dfrac{V}{3x^2} \right) = 6x^2 + \dfrac{8V}{3x}$.

To minimize $S$, differentiate with respect to $x$ and set to zero:

$\dfrac{dS}{dx} = 12x - \dfrac{8V}{3x^2} = 0$.

$12x = \dfrac{8V}{3x^2} \Rightarrow 36x^3 = 8V \Rightarrow V = \dfrac{36x^3}{8} = \dfrac{9x^3}{2}$.

Substitute $V$ back into the expression for $h$:

$h = \dfrac{9x^3 / 2}{3x^2} = \dfrac{3x}{2}$.

The height $h$ is $\dfrac{3}{2}$ times the shorter side of the base $x$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2} \times$ shorter side of base

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The side of an equilateral triangle expands at the rate of $\sqrt{3} \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm\sec$. When the side is $12 \mathrm{ cm}$, the rate of increase of its area is
questions.solution:
$A = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot a \cdot \dfrac{da}{dt}$

Substituting $a = 12$ cm and $\dfrac{da}{dt} = \sqrt{3}$ cm/sec:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 12 \times \sqrt{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} \times 12 \times \sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{36}{2} = 18$ cm^2/sec

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\text{ The point on the curve } x^2=x y \text{ which is closest to }(0,5) \text{$ is }
questions.solution:
The curve $x^2 = xy$ can be rewritten as $x(x-y) = 0$, giving two lines: $x = 0$ (y-axis) and $y = x$.

Checking if $(0,5)$ lies on the curve: substituting $x = 0$ gives $0 = 0$, which is satisfied.

So $(0,5)$ already lies on the curve (on the $x = 0$ branch), and the distance is exactly 0.

The closest point is $(0,5)$ itself.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For a given curve $y=2 x-x^2$, when $x$ increases at the rate of 3 units/sec, then how does the slope of the curve change?
questions.solution:
The equation of the curve is given by $y = 2x - x^2$.

The slope of the curve at any point $x$ is given by $m = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2 - 2x$.

To find the rate of change of the slope with respect to time $t$, we differentiate $m$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:

$\dfrac{dm}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(2 - 2x) = -2 \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

Given that the rate of increase of $x$ is $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 3$ units/sec, we substitute this value into the expression:

$\dfrac{dm}{dt} = -2 \times 3 = -6$ units/sec.

The negative sign indicates that the slope is decreasing at a rate of 6 units/sec.

questions.q: $f(x)=2 x-\tan ^{-1} x-\log (x+\sqrt{x^2+1}) \text{$ is monotonically increasing, when }
questions.solution:
The function is given by $f(x) = 2x - \tan^{-1} x - \log(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1})$.

To determine the interval where $f(x)$ is monotonically increasing, we find its derivative $f'(x)$ with respect to $x$.

$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(2x) - \dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan^{-1} x) - \dfrac{d}{dx}(\log(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1}))$.

The derivative of $\tan^{-1} x$ is $\dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}$.

The derivative of $\log(x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1})$ is $\dfrac{1}{x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1}} \times (1 + \dfrac{2x}{2\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}) = \dfrac{1}{x + \sqrt{x^2 + 1}} \times (\dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 1} + x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$.

Thus, $f'(x) = 2 - \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$.

Let $t = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}}$. Since $x^2 \ge 0$, we have $x^2 + 1 \ge 1$, so $0 < t \le 1$.

Then $\dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} = t^2$.

$f'(x) = 2 - t^2 - t = -(t^2 + t - 2) = -(t + 2)(t - 1) = (1 - t)(t + 2)$.

Since $0 < t \le 1$, $1 - t \ge 0$ and $t + 2 > 0$.

Therefore, $f'(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in R$. Specifically, $f'(x) = 0$ only at $t = 1$, which corresponds to $x = 0$.

Since $f'(x) > 0$ for $x \neq 0$ and $f(x)$ is continuous, $f(x)$ is monotonically increasing for all $x \in R$.

Answer: $x \in R$

questions.q: The function $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{2}{x}$ has a local minimum at
questions.solution:
Given the function $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{2}{x}$.

To find the local extrema, calculate the first derivative $f'(x)$:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left( \dfrac{x}{2} + 2x^{-1} \right) = \dfrac{1}{2} - 2x^{-2} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{2}{x^2}$.

Set $f'(x) = 0$ to find the critical points:

$\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{2}{x^2} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2}{x^2} \Rightarrow x^2 = 4 \Rightarrow x = \pm 2$.

Calculate the second derivative $f''(x)$ to determine the nature of the critical points:

$f''(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left( \dfrac{1}{2} - 2x^{-2} \right) = 0 - 2(-2)x^{-3} = \dfrac{4}{x^3}$.

Evaluate $f''(x)$ at the critical points:

For $x = 2$, $f''(2) = \dfrac{4}{2^3} = \dfrac{4}{8} = \dfrac{1}{2} > 0$. Since $f''(2) > 0$, the function has a local minimum at $x = 2$.

For $x = -2$, $f''(-2) = \dfrac{4}{(-2)^3} = \dfrac{4}{-8} = -\dfrac{1}{2} < 0$. Since $f''(-2) < 0$, the function has a local maximum at $x = -2$.

Answer: $x=2$

options: inversely proportional to its surface area
questions.solution:
The volume $V$ of a sphere of radius $r$ is given by $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4 \pi r^{2} \dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

It is given that the volume is increasing at a constant rate, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = k$, where $k$ is a positive constant.

Substituting this into the derivative equation, $k = 4 \pi r^{2} \dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

Solving for the rate of change of the radius, $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{k}{4 \pi r^{2}}$.

Since $4 \pi r^{2}$ is the surface area $S$ of the sphere, we have $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{k}{S}$.

This implies that the rate at which the radius is increasing is inversely proportional to the surface area of the sphere.

Answer: inversely proportional to its surface area

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $y + x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + a + b \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$.

Rearranging for $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, we have $\dfrac{dy}{dx} (x + b) = -(y + a)$, which implies $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{y + a}{x + b}$.

Equating the two expressions for $m$, we get $-\dfrac{1 + a}{1 + b} = 2$, which simplifies to $-(1 + a) = 2(1 + b)$, or $1 + a = -2 - 2b$, which gives $a + 2b = -3$.

Answer: $a=1, b=-2$

questions.q: The slant height of a cone is fixed at $7 \mathrm{~cm}$. If the rate of increase of its height is $0.3 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{sec}$, then the rate of increase of its volume when its height is $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ is
questions.solution:
We have, slant height of cone $(l)=7 \mathrm{~cm}$
$$
\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & l^{2}=h^{2}+r^{2} \quad \text{...(i)} \\
\Rightarrow & r^{2}=7^{2}-4^{2} \quad \text{[when h=4 cm]} \\
\Rightarrow & r^{2}=33 \\
\Rightarrow & r=\sqrt{33} \mathrm{~cm}
\end{array}
$$
Now, differentiating Eq. (i) w.r.t. $l$, we get
$$
\begin{gathered}
\quad 0=2 h \frac{d h}{d t}+2 r \frac{d r}{d t} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d r}{d t}=-\frac{h}{r} \frac{d h}{d t} \quad \text{...(ii)}  \\
\text { Volume of the cone, } V=\frac{1}{3} \pi r^{2} h \\
\frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{1}{3} \pi\left[2 r h \frac{d r}{d t}+r^{2} \frac{d h}{d t}\right] \\
\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{1}{3} \pi\left[2 r h\left(\frac{-h}{r} \frac{d h}{d t}\right)+r^{2} \frac{d h}{d t}\right](\text { from Eq. (ii)) } \\
\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{1}{3} \pi\left[-2 h^{2} \frac{d h}{d t}+r^{2} \frac{d h}{d t}\right] \\
\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d t}=\frac{1}{3} \pi \frac{d h}{d t}\left[-2 h^{2}+r^{2}\right] \\
\left.\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d t}\right]_{h=4} \quad=\frac{1}{3} \pi(0.3)\left[-2 \times 4^{2}+(\sqrt{33})^{2}\right] \\
\quad=\frac{\pi}{10}[1]=\frac{\pi}{10} \mathrm{cc} / \mathrm{sec}
\end{gathered}
$$

questions.q: The function $f(x)=5+36 x+3 x^{2}-2 x^{3}$ is increasing in the interval
questions.solution:
Given, $f(x)=5+36 x+3 x^{2}-2 x^{3}\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=36+6 x-6 x^{2}=-6\left(x^{2}-x-6\right)=-6\left(x^{2}-3 x+2 x-6\right)=-6(x-3)(x+2)$
For increasing function, $f^{\prime}(x) > 0\Rightarrow \quad(x-3)(x+2) < 0\Rightarrow \quad x < 3$ and $x > -2\Rightarrow \quad-2 < x < 3$
Hence, function $f(x)$ is increasing $\operatorname{in}(-2,3)$ interval.
